Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.

cat > docs/timers.md <<'EOF'
# Per-question timer

## Local settings and persistence

- `quizzes.timer_seconds` holds the full duration. The two number fields labelled
  **Timer minutes** and **Timer seconds** default to 0 and round-trip as quotient
  and remainder. Seconds above 59 are accepted and normalized. Negative,
  fractional, blank, nonnumeric and overflow inputs are rejected without writes;
  the maximum total is 2,147,483,647 seconds (well beyond any conference schedule).
- Games snapshot this duration when created, alongside questions and prize
  settings. Changes to the template apply to new games, not existing lobbies or
  ongoing games. Additive, idempotent migrations default old quizzes/games to 0.
- `games.opened_at_us`, already used for answer-speed scoring, is persisted each
  time Start/Next opens a question. The deadline is opening + duration. Reloads,
  reconnects and process restarts cannot reset it. A zero duration has no deadline.
- `transfer::QuizContents` deliberately has no timer field. Export is unchanged;
  imports get the database default (no timer), including imports from an export
  of a timed quiz. Extra hand-written timer JSON fields are ignored.

## Authoritative expiry

The server polls due open games every 100 ms, using a partial index that excludes
untimed and non-open games. It calls the same idempotent `finish_question`
transition as manual Finish, advancing phase to `closed` and incrementing version
and revision exactly once. It does not advance to the next question or end the
game. Results, counts, correct choices, scoring and prize behavior are unchanged.
Live subscribers receive the usual state notification.

Expiry is also checked while taking a snapshot or processing a moderator action
or answer, under the same database mutex as state transitions. Answers received
at or after the deadline are rejected even between worker ticks. Request-time
expiry runs before the action/answer transaction, so an invalid/stale request
cannot roll it back. The accepted answer's elapsed time uses the server timestamp
captured under that mutex, not a client-provided time.

On startup, an expiry sweep runs before binding the HTTP listener and reporting
readiness. The worker does not depend on any browser connection. Manual Finish
and auto-Finish share the same transition; a stale manual action at the deadline
gets the normal conflict response and refresh. There are no per-question queued
callbacks to accidentally finish a later question after an early Finish/Next.

## Display and privacy

Only moderator snapshots for an open timed question contain `timer`, with a
millisecond deadline and server clock sample. Player snapshots, including SSE
and initial HTML, have no timing metadata. A moderator-only `role="timer"`
element displays minutes and zero-padded seconds, with large tabular digits.

The client anchors the server's remaining interval to `performance.now()` rather
than its own wall clock. Every tick updates only the text node, not the question,
options or controls. A delayed sample cannot increase the displayed time for an
already-running question. No timer POSTs or per-second SSE messages are needed.
The server clock sample is omitted from SSE deduplication fingerprints. At zero,
the browser waits for the authoritative closed state; it never sends Finish.
The timer disappears in the lobby, on results, and after the game ends. The
countdown opts out of live-region announcements to avoid speaking every second.

## Verification

- `cargo test --offline --locked`: migrations, input validation/overflow, exact
  deadline boundary, idempotence, player privacy, rejected late answers/stale
  Finish, no-client worker, Next clock isolation, export exclusion, baseline app.
- `python3 tests/timer.py`: HTTP settings, frozen game duration, reload, auto/manual
  Finish, Next/last question, saved results, late answers, exports and disabled timer.
- `python3 tests/timer_browser.py`: real Chromium settings, 1:30/0:06 countdowns,
  reload continuity, player privacy/live feedback, stage disconnect and zero timer.
- `python3 tests/timer_persistence.py`: isolated storage and release process,
  restart before/after deadline, startup expiry before `/up`, and idle expiry
  verified directly in SQLite without any state endpoint/browser driving it.

The HTTP/browser tests use the existing test server credentials. The persistence
script builds offline and creates/removes its own temporary directory under
`storage/`. Browser screenshots also live under `storage/`.
